newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia announces incentives for offshore centre.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia announces incentives for offshore centre.

text.p: Banks based in Malaysia's offshore financial centre on Labuan island will be allowed to trade in ringgit-based instruments, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Monday.

The offshore banks would also be allowed to maintain their ringgit balances in interest-bearing external accounts, he announced at an Islamic banking conference in Labuan island, Malaysia's offshore financial centre offshore Borneo in the South China sea.

He said offshore banks would be allowed to trade in ringgit instruments in the secondary market to allow them greater access to ringgit business as well as to promote money market operations at the International Offshore Financial Centre.
"The banks are also allowed to purchase ringgit instruments in the primary market using foreign currency," said Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister.
In insurance, he said offshore life insurance companies would be allowed to sell investment-linked products to high net-worth Malaysians from a date to be announced later.
Offshore general insurance companies would also be allowed to underwrite domestic risks.

The businesses underwritten should be large and specialised risks of values exceeding 300 million ringgit, general liability risks of over 100 million ringgit and specialised liability risks valued at over 20 million ringgit but subject to certain conditions.

Anwar also announced that various allowances such as housing provided by employers to Malaysians in Labuan would be exempt from tax beginning in 1998 as part of measures to attract skilled Malaysians to work on the island.

He said the government will also be encouraging universities and institutions of higher learning to set up branches on the island to increase its population and generate a critical mass for greater economic activities.
